items.why: The W44 page says no pricing change was recorded; the latest change on it (Eleven v4 3x-credits promo ending, Oct 14) is already in the desk as an ended promo.
Base plan drops the 4,000 investigations per year per analyst cap for unlimited investigations and bundles three AI agents.

record.short: The base plan swaps the 4,000 investigations per year per analyst cap for unlimited investigations and bundles AI SOC Analyst, AI Threat Hunter and AI Threat Intel.

items.why: AI in Dropbox on Standard and Advanced loses chat Q&A, insights and content creation and gains organize, convert and undo tools; credits unchanged.

record.short: Standard and Advanced swap chat Q&A, insights and content creation for organize/rename, convert/compress/combine and approve/undo AI tools; credits stay at 250 and 750 a month.
record.deltaSub: AI tool list, Standard and Advanced
record.headline: Dropbox AI on Standard and Advanced no longer lists chat Q&A, file insights or content creation, and now lists organize and rename, convert, compress and combine, and approve and undo tools; monthly AI credits are unchanged.
rows: Ask questions in chat; insights; create content
Organize and rename; convert, compress, combine; approve and undo
record.who: Customers on the Standard and Advanced plans.
record.read: Dropbox appears to be steering its AI credits from conversational answers toward actions on files, which are easier to meter and demo. The credit pool did not change, so customers who used chat Q&A lose that use of it without compensation.
record.caveat: Based on the AI tool list on the pricing page; the page does not say whether chat Q&A moved elsewhere in the product.

items.why: New top Super plan (BETA) at $800 per agent per month above Executive.

record.short: Adds a BETA Super plan at $800 per agent per month above Executive, with a forward-deployed AE, agentic web prospecting and 20 Custom Smart Properties.

items.why: Credit cost per AI action moves from ranges to fixed amounts and new Teammates chats are metered at 5 credits each.

record.short: Credit costs per AI action move from ranges to fixed amounts (Q&A 5-10 → 8, email 2-5 → 4, run 16-24 → 20) and new Teammates chats on Growth cost 5 credits each.

items.why: Secret Key IP restrictions added to the comparison table, Business plan only; no existing price or entitlement changed.
Small Office Protection gains a 30-day no-payment trial option.
Contact-sales bundle table replaced by two self-serve per-state tiers at $79 and $69 a month plus a Custom tier.

record.short: The contact-sales bundle table (compliance package from $699) is replaced by Core Compliance at $79/state/month ($799/state/year) and Core Compliance + SST Services at $69/state/month ($699/state/year), plus a Custom tier for $50M+ revenue.

items.why: Translate language coverage grows from 15+ to 20+ languages; a capability list, not a plan quota or price.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Business shows $18.00 per user per month against $21.00 a week earlier and is now labelled an add-on.

record.short: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business shows $18.00 per user per month, down from $21.00, and is now labelled as an add-on.
record.deltaSub: Copilot Business add-on, per user per month
record.headline: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business now shows $18.00 per user per month instead of $21.00 and carries an add-on label, making clear it needs an existing Microsoft 365 plan.
rows: Copilot Business, per user per month
record.who: Customers buying Copilot Business on top of an existing Microsoft 365 plan.
record.read: The add-on label positions Copilot Business as an upsell to the base licence, and the lower figure, if it is the list price, makes that upsell cheaper. The 14% size is calculated from the two captured figures.
record.caveat: The two captures show $21.00 and then $18.00, but the source's own summary describes the price as unchanged after a relabel, so the cut is unconfirmed until we capture the Microsoft page ourselves.
